title: Is the subsample built at open still the right way to search with a max query length?
body:
`count`, `extract` and `locate` take `-m`/`--max-query-len`, which limits how many characters of a query a search compares. When the suffixes are opened in memory and that limit is shorter than the sort, `typed::open` in `libsufr/src/typed.rs` keeps the whole suffix array on disk and holds a subsample in memory instead. A search runs over the subsample and maps a hit back to ranks in the whole array.

The subsample is a `Subsample<W>`: the first suffix of each group that shares its first `max_query_len` characters, and that suffix's rank in the whole array. `TypedSuffixArray::subsample` builds it. With an LCP array it reads the LCP array in blocks and keeps a suffix whose LCP is below `max_query_len`. Without one, `subsample_by_text` calls `keep_differing`, which reads the suffix array in blocks and compares each suffix with the one before it, by the text or by the care positions under a seed mask. `subsample_with_cache` writes the result to `~/.sufr/locate-<max_query_len>-<basename>` and reads it back on a later open, unless the `.sufr` file is newer than the cache file.

Commit b3f9104 removed the build-time max query length, so an unmasked file is now always sorted on its full suffixes. `Header::sorted_len` is the text length for such a file, and any `-m` from 1 to below the text length on it now builds a subsample. The subsampling code was written when a capped build was the usual way to use `-m`, and nobody has reviewed it since that commit.

## Open

- Whether subsampling should stay at all. Building it reads every suffix and, without an LCP array, compares the text at each one. No one has timed that on a genome-sized file. The alternative is to search the whole array and stop comparing at `max_query_len`.
- Whether the in-memory subsample is worth the switch to a disk suffix array that the caller did not ask for. A caller who opens the suffixes in memory gets them on disk when `-m` is given.
- The cache key holds the file's basename and not its path, so two files with one name in different directories share a cache file. The mtime check guards only against a `.sufr` file newer than the cache.
- Whether a cache belongs in the library. Where it is written is sufr-22b9c3. The race on creating its directory, sufr-742f13, was fixed in 8f3d833, which creates the directory with `create_dir_all`.
- Which tests pin subsampled results against an unsubsampled search, with and without an LCP array and under a mask. `test_subsample_suffix_array` in `libsufr/src/lib.rs` checks the subsample itself.

notes.author: Jeb Rosen/64259a5a
notes.text:
Measured with `bench_subsample`, an ignored test in `libsufr/src/bench_subsample.rs` (a2aa3ba on branch `worktree-subsample-bench`). For each max query length m it opens one file four ways, with the text in memory each time:

- sub-cold: the subsample built at open, with no cache file
- sub-warm: the subsample read back from its cache file
- full-mem: no subsample, the whole suffix array in memory, comparisons stopping at m
- full-disk: no subsample, the whole suffix array on disk

All four returned the same ranks for every query. The queries are 1M windows of length m from random all-ACGT positions in the text, one in ten replaced by a random ACGT string. A count is `matching_ranks` alone, run on one thread and on a 32-thread rayon pool. Host catalyst, file in page cache.

hg38 built with `sufr create -d`, no LCP array, 3,049,315,784 suffixes, 4-byte ints:

| m | config | open s | suffixes searched | held GiB | count us/q | 32 threads us/q |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | sub-cold | 18.0 | 71,019 | 0.0005 | 1.20 | 0.094 |
| 8 | sub-warm | 1.7 | 71,019 | 0.0005 | 1.18 | 0.063 |
| 8 | full-mem | 8.2 | 3,049,315,784 | 11.4 | 5.88 | 0.211 |
| 8 | full-disk | 1.6 | 3,049,315,784 | 0 | 60.3 | 39.0 |
| 12 | sub-cold | 19.1 | 16,624,396 | 0.12 | 3.35 | 0.162 |
| 12 | sub-warm | 1.7 | 16,624,396 | 0.12 | 3.35 | 0.125 |
| 12 | full-mem | 8.2 | 3,049,315,784 | 11.4 | 6.53 | 0.251 |
| 16 | sub-cold | 35.2 | 1,135,813,622 | 8.5 | 5.56 | 0.254 |
| 16 | sub-warm | 5.8 | 1,135,813,622 | 8.5 | 5.74 | 0.226 |
| 16 | full-mem | 8.1 | 3,049,315,784 | 11.4 | 5.61 | 0.232 |
| 32 | sub-cold | 37.6 | 2,575,402,853 | 19.2 | 6.63 | 0.276 |
| 32 | sub-warm | 11.9 | 2,575,402,853 | 19.2 | 6.39 | 0.245 |
| 32 | full-mem | 8.1 | 3,049,315,784 | 11.4 | 5.91 | 0.217 |

full-disk counts took 57 to 61 us on one thread and 37 to 39 us on 32 threads at every m. The open time of full-disk is loading the text alone.

chr1 (230,481,013 suffixes) shows the same pattern. The subsample keeps 66,396 suffixes at m=8 and 13,964,965 at m=12, against 166 M at m=16 and 209 M at m=32. Without the cache it took 0.85 to 2.5 s to build, or 0.53 to 2.3 s from an LCP array. At m=16 and above it held 1.4 to 1.8 times the memory of the whole array.

What the numbers say:

- A kept suffix carries its rank, so the subsample takes less memory than the whole array only when it keeps under half of the suffixes. On DNA that means 4^m well below the suffix count: m of 12 or less on both files. There it wins on memory, open time and count time, by 2 to 5 times per count.
- At m=32 the subsample is worse than full-mem on every measure. `typed::open` takes it for any m below the text length on an unmasked file.
- The cache file changes the open time only. Against full-mem at m=8 on hg38, a session without the cache needs about 2.1M one-thread counts, or about 84M on 32 threads, before the faster counts make up the 9.8 s extra open. At m=12 the figures are 3.4M and 122M.
- Dropping the subsample means keeping the whole array in memory. Searching it on disk, which `typed::open` switches to under the subsample, is 10 to 50 times slower per count and gains little from more threads.
- The locate time follows the hit count and differs little across the four.

I lean to keeping the subsample only when it is much smaller than the array, and otherwise searching the whole array in memory with comparisons stopping at m. One way to choose is to compare the alphabet size to the m-th power against the suffix count before building. Another is to build it and drop it when it keeps over half of the suffixes.
